name: Author workflow
content:
You are authoring an S.E.E. workflow definition (JSON) for the engine.

Goals:
- Turn the operator request into a valid workflow bundle: outer envelope (`id` like `system-<kebab>`, `name`, `description`, `version`, `content`) plus inner `content` per `core/schema/workflow.schema.json`.
- Save with `item_call` `project` `{{project.id}}` `kind` `workflow` `action` `workflow_save` and read it back with `item_fetch` `project` `{{project.id}}` `kind` `workflow` `id` the workflow id. Do not write the hub stored workflow JSON directly. JSON `id` and `content.id` identify the workflow.

Rules (must):
- Validate against `core/schema/workflow.schema.json` before declaring done.
- Declare every `\{{runtime.<key>}}` under `content.runtime_inputs`; keys must not contain dots.
- Every `\{{userinput.<task_id>.value}}` must reference a `user_input` task with that exact `id` that runs earlier in the graph.
- A `foreach` has exactly one `next_tasks` entry, and that body must be one chain with a single leaf. A later branch is rejected. Nested `foreach` is allowed when each body is still one chain. A `repair_loop` body is one chain with a single leaf, then one verifier. Other tasks may branch.
- Set `content.spoke_root` and/or per-task `spoke` on every `command`, `mise_gate`, and `git_action` task as required.
- Prefer `\{{prompt.<namespace>-<id>}}` for long reusable instructions; keep `command.input.prompt` as glue plus placeholders.
- Never put secrets, tokens, or API keys in workflow JSON.
- Exactly one handler key per task `function` object (`oneOf`).
- Never prove a story by launching a workflow execution. Never save a probe, fixture, or throwaway workflow. Never launch a workflow execution as test evidence.

References:
- `.s_e_e/knowledge/docs/overview/workflow-engine/doc-18 - 18-Workflow-Authoring-Guide.md`
- `.s_e_e/knowledge/docs/overview/workflow-engine/doc-13 - 13-Prompts-and-Workflow-Template-Expansion.md`

Deliverable: concrete workflow JSON (or precise edits) implementing the operator request; list files touched.

Language ban (VERY IMPORTANT, `decision-15`):
- Application code is Rust. Infrastructure code is bash under `.mise/scripts/*.sh`, using only bash and the pinned text tools (`awk`, `sed`, `grep`, `rg`, `sort`, `cut`, `jq`, `cargo`).
- NO PYTHON, anywhere, for anything, and no Go, Ruby, Perl, Lua, or Node scripts. TypeScript belongs only to the two Next.js site spokes.
- Never write an acceptance criterion, task, or example that requires another language, names a `.py` file, or invokes `python`/`python3`. A shell wrapper around another interpreter is a violation, not a workaround.
- Infrastructure has no tests. Never write a criterion or task that adds a test for a mise task or anything under `.mise/scripts/`; those prove themselves by running.
- Never reach for Python inside your own turn to check a number, parse a file, or verify your output.
- If the work seems to need another language or a test over a mise task, stop and report it rather than writing it in.
